chapter: Las Vegas, Sinatra and later years
title: Recovering pitch; Eve's death and returning at Caesar's Palace
summary: His pitch drifted but his hearing adjusted and he lost the fear of playing; after Eve died he sat out two years until Vegas friends got him to Caesar's Palace.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well I was just trying to get over that. I felt I'd disappointed Gibson, you know. If I didn't go on. And, so -- I don't know, they seemed to think that I got through it all right. I guess I gained a little confidence from it, cause I went back home and I started playing a little bit, tried to play. It was very disheartening, I could go -- like my pitch at both ends of the -- at the higher level, would go flat, and

the bottom level was off, I didn't have a -- it's gradually came back and I identify a little better now, but it's been years doing it. I think your mind -- I don't know how to say this, but I think your mind finally adjusts to different -- your hearing adjusts. Now I don't have any problems now.
Ah --
I don't hear real high, in other words, things go flat if I was too high.
Yeah.
But I've lost the fear of playing.
Yeah, you -- you know how to -- how to cope under various conditions, now, I mean you've done it long enough now that you --
Yeah.
You know how to adlib and -- you know.
Well I think I went through a period where I didn't, you know what I'm saying?
Yeah.
I think I went through a period where the pianos were 10 feet from me, I would have problems.
Yeah.
I couldn't hear them well.
Yeah.
Little things.
Yeah.
That would normally not -- course I think anybody that's 12 or 15 feet from a piano, can be bothered.
Sure.
I found out it wasn't only me, that I was taking a lot for granted and blaming it on my hearing where I shouldn't have -- I should have (inaudible).
Yeah.
So I realized that I had to go and -- but now, I'm going around, playing with different groups. I don't have a group of my own, go from place to place, they have great trios --

It seems to me that more remarkable than ever. You don't have your own group, you're exposed to different musicians all the time and you cope, I mean it shows you that you're pretty well in the saddle.
Well I think I got over the big problem of the hearing to a certain extent.
Yeah, yeah.
So there's always a little underlying fear that something else might happen --
Since when --
-- because, actually now, after I when Eve left I didn't play for a couple of years and I really thought I wouldn't play. I didn't feel like playing and then
I went up to Vegas and met some people in the hotel, they and said, "You can't be that way." So I went to work at Caesar's Palace for about 20 weeks, it was fun.
Yeah.
